pages.html:
INC-PAY-001 — Payment-service incident overview

Fictional hackathon data. Incident date: 2026-09-28. Service: payment-service. Severity: SEV-2. Incident commander: Maya Tan. Status: Resolved; follow-up work remains.

Summary

Payment requests timed out between 14:10 and 15:02 SGT after a configuration rollout increased concurrent database connections beyond the available pool. The on-call team rolled back the configuration and verified recovery.

Where to find details

  • Confluence: recovery runbook, postmortem, timeline, customer impact, follow-up actions, and incident response policy in the PAYOPS space.
  • Jira: PAY-101, PAY-102, PAY-103. Jira is authoritative for current ticket status.
  • Slack: #payment-incident-001. Slack contains the live discussion and threaded updates.
  • Google Drive: INC-PAY-001 payment metrics report. The file contains supporting charts and exports.

Use INC-PAY-001 as the shared correlation key in all four platforms.

pages.title: Payment-service recovery runbook
pages.html:
Payment-service recovery runbook

Fictional hackathon data. Owner: Payments SRE. Applies to: INC-PAY-001 and similar payment-service database connection saturation incidents. Status: Current. Reviewed: 2026-09-28 16:00 SGT.

Symptoms

Elevated payment timeout rate, database connection pool at capacity, and falling successful authorization rate.

Recovery procedure — version 1

  1. Declare the incident and identify the active payment-service deployment.
  2. Pause further payment-service configuration rollouts.
  3. Roll back the connection-limit change to the last known good configuration.
  4. Watch connection utilization, timeout rate, and successful authorization rate for ten minutes.
  5. Record the recovery decision in INC-PAY-001 and notify the incident channel.

If rollback does not restore service, escalate to the incident commander and database on-call engineer before attempting failover. Do not treat an unverified Slack suggestion as an approved runbook step.

pages.title: INC-PAY-001 — Payment-service postmortem
pages.html:
INC-PAY-001 — Payment-service postmortem

Fictional hackathon data. Written 2026-09-28 17:30 SGT. Owner: Maya Tan. Status: Confirmed technical findings; follow-up actions open.

Confirmed root cause

A payment-service configuration rollout at 14:07 SGT raised the maximum number of application database connections. Under production traffic, the aggregate connection demand exceeded the database pool limit. Requests queued and timed out. This conclusion is supported by the rollout event, connection metrics, and recovery after rollback.

Impact

Payment requests saw elevated timeout errors from 14:10 to 15:02 SGT. The customer impact page and Google Drive metrics report contain the quantified impact.

Recovery

The team paused rollouts at 14:24, began rollback at 14:37, and confirmed normal success rate at 15:02. Use the current recovery runbook for any repeat incident.

Open work

PAY-101 caps connection settings and adds rollout validation. PAY-102 adds saturation alerts. PAY-103 rehearses failover and updates the runbook. Jira owns current status and assignees.

Uncertainty

The exact share of failed customer payment attempts is pending reconciliation with the final metrics export. Do not state a final failure count from this page alone.

pages.title: INC-PAY-001 — Customer impact
pages.html:
INC-PAY-001 — Customer impact

Fictional hackathon data. Impact window: 2026-09-28 14:10–15:02 SGT. Regions: Singapore and Malaysia payment traffic. Owner: Payments Analytics.

During the window, payment authorization success fell below its normal baseline and timeout errors increased. A preliminary estimate is 1,240 timed-out attempts; this number is provisional until reconciliation completes.

Supporting source: Google Drive file titled INC-PAY-001 payment metrics report, containing minute-level success-rate and timeout charts. The Drive owner will supply the actual file link when available.

Do not infer a final affected-customer count from this summary.

pages.title: INC-PAY-001 — Follow-up actions
pages.html:
INC-PAY-001 — Follow-up actions

Fictional hackathon data. This page explains why each action exists. Jira is authoritative for current owner, status, and due date.

  • PAY-101: Cap payment-service connection settings and validate them during rollout.
  • PAY-102: Alert earlier on database connection saturation and elevated payment timeouts.
  • PAY-103: Rehearse failover and revise the recovery runbook based on the exercise.

All three tickets were created after INC-PAY-001. Query Jira for their live status before answering what work remains.

pages.title: Payment incident response policy
pages.html:
Payment incident response policy

Fictional hackathon data. Owner: Payments SRE. Reviewed: 2026-09-20.

Roles

The on-call engineer may declare an incident and begin documented mitigation. The incident commander approves a production failover. The database on-call engineer verifies database health. The communications lead publishes customer-facing updates.

Evidence and decisions

Record major decisions with timestamps and links to the incident ID. Use the current runbook for recovery steps, the postmortem for confirmed cause, Jira for live follow-up status, and metrics reports for quantitative impact.

Do not turn an unverified discussion message into an approved recovery instruction.
